title: Retail Sales Performance Report 2023-2024
executive_summary: Verified analysis of the cleaned retail order data shows total 2023-2024 revenue of $445,325.09 across 520 orders, with an average order value of $856.39. Revenue grew 10.08% year over year, from $211,976.29 in 2023 to $233,348.80 in 2024. The East region is the strongest performer and the South the weakest. Within 2024, revenue climbed steadily to a Q3 peak before a modest Q4 dip. Order revenue is heavily right-skewed: a few large orders pull the mean ($856.39) well above the median ($313.28). Customer concentration is low, with the top customer accounting for only 6.24% of revenue, and high-discount Electronics orders (22 orders) contribute about 11.24% of total revenue.

key_findings.statement: Overall performance: total revenue reached $445,325.09 across 520 orders in 2023-2024, giving an average order value of $856.39.
Regional comparison: the East region leads with $130,516.69, followed by North ($124,845.75), West ($99,428.16) and South ($90,534.49); East exceeds South by $39,982.20.

2024 quarterly trend: revenue built through the year from a low of $36,108.31 in Q1, rising to $56,616.79 in Q2 and peaking at $71,674.99 in Q3, before easing slightly to $68,948.71 in Q4; Q3 exceeded Q1 by $35,566.68.
Year-over-year change: revenue increased from $211,976.29 in 2023 to $233,348.80 in 2024, a growth of 10.08%.
High-discount Electronics: 22 orders had a discount of 20% or more, generating $50,035.33 in revenue, equivalent to about 11.24% of total revenue.

Order revenue distribution is strongly right-skewed: the mean ($856.39) is roughly 2.73 times the median ($313.28), with a large standard deviation of $1,295.74 and values ranging from a minimum of $5.27 to a maximum of $7,844.02.
Customer concentration is low: 222 unique customers placed orders, and the highest-revenue customer contributed $27,793.13, just 6.24% of total revenue, indicating no single-customer dependency.

limitations: The data covers only 2023-2024, so longer-term trends and seasonality beyond one year cannot be assessed.
Analysis is revenue-based only; no cost, margin or profit figures are available, so growth may not equate to profitability.
The strong right skew (mean far above median) means average order value overstates the typical order; headline figures are influenced by a small number of large orders.
Regional results are aggregated to four broad regions and may mask variation at store or city level.
The high-discount Electronics view captures only orders at 20%+ discount and does not show the margin impact of that discounting.
conclusion: The business delivered solid, broad-based growth in 2024 (+10.08% YoY), with momentum peaking in Q3. East and North drive the majority of revenue, while the South lags and may warrant targeted investment. Revenue is diversified across 222 customers with no concentration risk, but the skewed order distribution suggests focusing on growing mid-sized orders rather than relying on occasional large deals. High-discount Electronics orders are a meaningful revenue stream (about 11.24% of total) whose profitability should be monitored.
